mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of periods with sustained HOUST increases, or the correlation between HOUST growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased wage pressures and inflation expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% within the last month signals a strengthening consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals an inflationary environment with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a tightening labor market with strong job growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decrease on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter indicates a strengthening economy, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of periods with sustained GDPC1 increases, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
